summary: REFUTE stage fan-out: the Level selects the required independent adversaries. DRY runs at every Level; L1 runs all five, L2 runs Prove-It, DRY, and Lie-catcher with optional Laziness-auditor, and L3 runs DRY with an optional human-requested Lie-catcher. Produces one verdict per required lens; any FAIL blocks the gate.

findings.summary: The contract's explicit, repeated requirement to retain command output in the work folder was not fulfilled for the dotnet-restore/NuGetAudit verification and the PDB SourceLink check (Acceptance 8 and 11), and for the make build/make test run (Acceptance 3) — the folder retains only status/diff/snapshot bookkeeping, never the command output itself, so nothing in the delivered change lets a reviewer confirm these criteria without redoing the work.
findings.evidence: Contract text, quoted verbatim: Acceptance 3 — "`make build` and `make test` pass. Retain exact commands and output." Acceptance 11 — "The debugging symbols for a built assembly still carry the SourceLink source mapping. Establish it from the built PDB rather than from the build log." Step 7 — "REMAINING — run the analyzer suite, then `make build` and `make test`, retaining exact commands and output." Step 9 — "REMAINING — verify `dotnet restore`, `make build`, and `make test` all pass with NuGet auditing enabled and no command-line override, and that the built debugging symbols still carry the SourceLink source mapping." Decisions (final round) — "Save command output, reviewer results, snapshot identities, and the final changed-file list in the current work folder." Absence, confirmed two ways: `ls -la .dev/inprocess/74-pre-work-move-system-services/` lists only adjudication.md, contract-analyzer-runner-repair.md, contract.md, final-snapshot-id.txt, final-status.txt, final-tracked.patch, final-untracked-AnalyzerRunnerTests.cs.snapshot, hidden-decision-scan.json, issue.md, repair-baseline-analyzer-tests.txt, repair-baseline-diff.patch, repair-baseline-status.txt — every one of these is git-status/diff/snapshot-identity text, none is build, test, restore, or PDB output. A repo-wide `find . -type f -newermt "2026-09-12 12:00:00" -not -path "*/.git/*" -not -path "*/bin/*" -not -path "*/obj/*" -not -path "*/TestResults/*"` (run from the repo root) returns the same file list plus only the 12 changed source/props files — no log/output/txt artifact for a build, test, restore, or PDB inspection exists anywhere in the tree. This is despite the SAME round diligently retaining sibling artifacts (final-status.txt, final-snapshot-id.txt, final-tracked.patch) per the identical Decision sentence, which makes the absence of the command-output half conspicuous rather than an intentional design choice. I independently reran every one of these checks myself, in an isolated git worktree at the exact reviewed snapshot (HEAD e30c257eb45962721b5320ab59110d148c533503, matching final-snapshot-id.txt; tree verified byte-identical to final-tracked.patch and final-untracked-AnalyzerRunnerTests.cs.snapshot before running anything), and every one passes: `make build` -> "Build succeeded. 0 Warning(s) 0 Error(s)", exit 0; `make test` -> AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests.dll 438/438, AgentGuard.CrossPlatform.Tests.dll 56/56, AgentGuard.Cli.Tests.dll 11/11, AgentGuard.Tests.dll 148/148, exit 0; `dotnet restore` at both project and solution scope exits 0 with no NU-prefixed diagnostic in the output; `dotnet msbuild analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests.csproj -getProperty:NuGetAudit -getProperty:NuGetAuditMode -getProperty:NuGetAuditLevel` returns `{"Properties":{"NuGetAudit":"true","NuGetAuditMode":"all","NuGetAuditLevel":"low"}}`, confirming auditing is genuinely on rather than silently disabled; `strings -a analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/bin/Debug/net10.0/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests.pdb | grep -i sourcelink` returns the literal embedded SourceLink document `{"documents":{".../*":"https://raw.githubusercontent.com/4thWAIV/agent-guard/e30c257eb45962721b5320ab59110d148c533503/*"}}`, read directly from the PDB bytes and naming the exact reviewed commit. So every underlying claim is factually true right now, but the delivered artifact itself retains none of this proof — of the three, Acceptance 11's PDB byte-inspection and Acceptance 8's specific NuGetAudit-property/no-NU1902 verification are the sharpest gap, since neither is a byproduct any later standard step (e.g. GATE's generic closing `make build`+`make test` bracket) would automatically regenerate; only a deliberate save closes them.
findings.fix: Persist this proof into the work folder now, e.g. `final-build-test-output.txt` (the make build + make test transcript with exit codes), `final-restore-output.txt` (the dotnet restore transcript plus the `-getProperty` NuGetAudit/NuGetAuditMode values), and `final-pdb-sourcelink.txt` (the `strings`/PDB extract showing the embedded SourceLink document). No code change is required — every check already passes on the exact reviewed snapshot, verbatim above — so this is a pure retention fix, not another implementation round.

findings.summary: The comment correction the contract mandates in NoTimeoutInPresenceImplAnalyzerTests.cs replaced a false statement with a different false statement: the new class comment asserts that EVERY fixture in the class implements IPresenceCheck and must supply Check, which is untrue for four of the nine fixtures and is directly contradicted by another comment in the same file. This re-creates the exact failure mode the contract exists to repair — a comment that tells the next reader something about the fixtures that is not true.
findings.evidence:
Live file /Users/timothystockstill/code/macos/4thWAIV/agent-guard/analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/NoTimeoutInPresenceImplAnalyzerTests.cs:16-18 reads "Every fixture here implements IPresenceCheck in full: each presence class supplies the interface's Check method, because the analyzer runner requires each fixture to produce exactly the compiler errors its call site declares and these call sites declare none." and lines 21-23 read "The one IPresenceCheck member every fixture in this class must supply, spelled once and interpolated into each fixture below."

The class has nine [Fact] fixtures (lines 29, 53, 76, 101, 130, 155, 178, 198, 218). Only five interpolate {{PresenceCheckMember}} (lines 40, 64, 88, 114, 207). The other four declare no IPresenceCheck implementer at all: line 142 `internal sealed class MacLocalAuthentication : ILocalAuthentication`, line 166 `internal sealed class TmdsPolkitAuthority : IPolkitAuthority`, line 187 `internal sealed class Ordinary`, line 230 `internal sealed class ObjCRuntime : IObjCRuntime`.

The same file contradicts itself at line 180, inside TimeoutOutsidePresenceImpl_IsNotReported: "A class that does NOT implement IPresenceCheck is not this rule's concern (AG0038 governs its waits)." That fixture's entire purpose is a class that does not implement IPresenceCheck, so "every fixture in this class must supply" Check is disproven by the fixture three lines below the claim.

Commands run against the live tree: `grep -n "public async Task|IPresenceCheck|PresenceCheckMember|internal sealed class" analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/NoTimeoutInPresenceImplAnalyzerTests.cs`; `sed -n '13,30p'` and `sed -n '176,196p'` on the same file.

Contract basis: Decisions — "Correct the runner comments and failure wording"; Surfaces — "`NoTimeoutInPresenceImplAnalyzerTests.cs` — five fixtures, CS0535, and the class comment that states those fixtures omit `Check`." The correction was scoped to the five repaired fixtures; the text written generalizes it to all nine and is false. Acceptance 4b's literal grep (`grep -rn "compile error is irrelevant\|without supplying"`) returns nothing (verified, exit 1), so the pinned check passes while the replacement text is still untrue.

findings.evidence:
The pre-change class comment stated the file's rule (git diff of analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/SharedAnalyzerSources.cs, removed lines): "C# source snippets shared verbatim by more than one analyzer test class, held in one place so a byte-identical fixture is not spelled twice."

`grep -rn "SystemServicesContainerMembers\|FileSystemContainerMembers\|PlatformServicesContainerMembers" analyzers/AgentGuard.Analyzers.Tests/*.cs` plus the enclosing test methods gives the actual usage:
- SystemServicesContainerMembers — ContainerInterfaceSingleOwnerAnalyzerTests.cs:57,61 (SecondImplementerOfContainer_IsReported, line 47), :82 (SingleImplementerOfContainer_IsNotReported, line 74), :102,106 (SecondImplementerOfContainer_InTestAssembly_IsStillReported_NoExemption, line 91) — three tests, claim holds.
- FileSystemContainerMembers — :127 and :131, both inside SecondImplementerOfSubContainer_IsReported (line 118) — ONE test.
- PlatformServicesContainerMembers — :135 and :139, both inside that same SecondImplementerOfSubContainer_IsReported — ONE test.

No other test class references any of the three (grep returns only ContainerInterfaceSingleOwnerAnalyzerTests.cs and SharedAnalyzerSources.cs itself), so none of the three meets the file's original "more than one analyzer test class" rule, and two do not meet the softened "more than one test" replacement either. The parallel case in the same change was handled the opposite way: PresenceCheckMember (NoTimeoutInPresenceImplAnalyzerTests.cs:24) is a private const kept local to its one consuming class, so the same kind of single-class member was placed under two different owners in one change.
